takeaways: When a page makes a legal commitment or financial transaction, changes or deletes user data, or submits test answers, mistakes must be fixable.
Do at least one: make the action reversible, check the input and let people correct errors, or show a review step to confirm before final submission.
A review screen before “Pay” or “Sign”, an undo after “Delete”, or a cancellation period all count.
Other forms are not covered by this AA rule, though the same patterns help everywhere.
failures: A one-tap purchase with no review and no cancel
Delete with no confirm and no undo
A test that submits answers the moment the last one is picked
check: List every action in the flow that spends money, signs something, changes saved data or submits a test.
For each, point to the screen or state that gives the second chance.
Check the review step shows what will actually happen: amount, item, recipient.

quiz.question: A banking app sends a transfer as soon as people tap “Send”. What is the lightest fix that meets the rule?
options: A review screen with the amount and payee, and a “Confirm” button
A help article explaining how to call support
quiz.why: A chance to review and confirm before final submission meets the rule. A toast confirms after the fact and reverses nothing.

spec: Mark each covered action and which safeguard it uses: undo, check, or confirm.
Design the review screen and the undo state, with how long undo stays available.
Write what the confirm button says, so it names the action, like “Pay £40”.
review: If I tapped this by mistake, how would I get back?
Does the review step show the details that matter?
Which actions here change saved data, and are they covered?
tradeoff: Extra steps slow down frequent users. Undo often beats a confirm dialog: it is fast for the confident and safe for everyone else.
system: Provide a review screen pattern and an undoable delete pattern, and point to them from every destructive or payment component.
pitch: A second chance before money moves costs one screen. A mistaken payment costs a complaint, a refund and trust.
